prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.

worlds.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The flyer's figure of fourteen hundred dollars was exactly what families were billed, once, when their child enrolled. In a district where the typical household earned under thirty thousand dollars a year, only a third of students arrived with a laptop that fall, and families who had paid got nothing back when their children graduated. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
worlds.explanation: In a low-income district, only a third of students could get the laptop, so the charge was "prohibitive." "Recurring" fails because it was billed once. "Refundable" fails because families got nothing back, and "misleading" fails because the flyer's figure was exactly what was billed.

recurring.why: a one-time charge does not recur

worlds.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The flyer listed eighty dollars, and that was exactly what families were billed in September; nearly every family paid it. The following September every family received the same eighty-dollar bill, and the September after that, until the child graduated and the laptop, by then worn out, stayed with the family. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
worlds.explanation: The same bill came every September until graduation, so the charge was "recurring." "Prohibitive" fails because nearly every family paid it. "Refundable" fails because families simply kept the worn-out laptop with no money returned, and "misleading" fails because the flyer's figure was exactly what was billed.

prohibitive.why: the charge did not keep families out

refundable.why: no money came back at the end

worlds.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The flyer listed two hundred dollars, and families were billed exactly that, once, when their child enrolled; nearly every family paid it. At graduation, students who handed back working laptops found a check for two hundred dollars tucked into their diploma folders. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
worlds.explanation: Families got their money back when the laptops were returned, so the charge was "refundable." "Prohibitive" fails because nearly every family paid it. "Recurring" fails because it was billed once, and "misleading" fails because families were billed exactly the flyer's figure.

prohibitive.why: the charge did not keep families out

recurring.why: a one-time charge does not recur

worlds.passage: In 2022 one public high school began requiring every student to use a laptop bought through its own program. The flyer listed two hundred dollars, a sum nearly every family paid, once, when their child enrolled. On the first day, students learned that the laptop would not start without a case, software, and insurance sold only by the school, which together cost four hundred dollars more; families grumbled, paid, and never saw that money again. For most families, the laptop charge the school had announced turned out to be ______.
worlds.explanation: The flyer's figure left out required extras costing twice as much, so the announced charge was "misleading." "Prohibitive" fails because nearly every family paid, extras included. "Recurring" fails because it was paid once, and "refundable" fails because families never saw the money again.

prohibitive.why: the charge did not keep families out

recurring.why: a one-time charge does not recur
